root_cause: WPC surface bulletin coordinate tokens are assumed to contain only an optional leading minus sign followed by digits before they are split into latitude and longitude. Archived CODSUS products sometimes contain stray punctuation or letters inside otherwise valid coordinate fields, so the parser attempts to build floats from malformed lat/lon substrings and raises ValueError instead of recovering the numeric coordinate.
approach: Sanitize coordinate tokens inside _decode_coords by preserving an initial minus sign for southern hemisphere latitude and removing all other non-digit characters before the existing split/float logic runs. Add a compact regression sample that includes punctuation and letter contamination in front coordinates to verify parse_wpc_surface_bulletin still returns the expected geometry.
tests_to_add: Extend WPC surface bulletin parser regression coverage for malformed coordinate tokens such as 411"45 and I4222.
risk_notes: Overly permissive sanitizing may turn a severely malformed token into a plausible coordinate instead of rejecting it.
out_of_scope_observations: Malformed front labels such as TRmOF being silently ignored could merit a warning, but that is separate from the coordinate parsing crash.
